newsitem.title: UK: Opposition say 19 arrested in Bahrain, Kuwait.
newsitem.headline: Opposition say 19 arrested in Bahrain, Kuwait.

text.p: A Bahraini opposition group on Saturday alleged that 19 Bahraini Shi'ite Moslems including children had been arrested this week in Bahrain and Kuwait.

The Bahrain Freedom Movement said in a statement sent to an international news organisation that Bahrain had arrested eight people including 15-year-old Ahmed Salman Hassan, 15, from Bani Jamrah village, 12 km (7.5 miles) west of the capital Manama.

Two children, Sayed Hussain Hamid, 8, and his brother Sayed Mohammad, 9, were arrested and beaten before being released, the statement said. Another three people from the Shi'ite village of Karzakkan had been tortured, it said, but gave no details.
The group said Kuwait had also arrested 11 Bahrainis in the Hawally area.
"An armed group attacked two flats in (the) Hawally area and arrested Bahraini citizens," the London-based group said.
"During the attack, police had damaged everything in the flats such as televisions, videos and refrigerators," it said. The allegations could not be immediately confirmed.
Bahrain's State Security Court this week jailed 36 Shi'ite Moslems accused of involvement in an alleged pro-Iranian plot to topple the government by force. It also acquitted 23 suspects.

Members of the island's majority Shi'ite Moslem community have waged sporadic protests, bombings, arson attacks and violence since December 1994 to demand political and economic reforms by the Sunni-led government.
Around 28 people have been killed and hundreds arrested, including children.
